summary: This note covers two aspects of Australia. The first describes its government: state and territory parliaments, which are unicameral or bicameral, the heads of government and the Queen's representatives, and the external territories administered directly by the Commonwealth Parliament. The second describes Australian literature and performing arts, from 19th-century bush writers and Booker and Nobel winners to opera, ballet and state theatre companies.
one_line: Overview of Australia's state and territory governments, external territories, and its literature and performing arts.
key_facts: Unicameral parliaments exist in the Northern Territory, the ACT and Queensland; the other states have bicameral parliaments.
In the states the lower houses are known as the Legislative Assembly, except in South Australia and Tasmania, where they are the House of Assembly.
The head of government in each state is the Premier, and in each territory it is the Chief Minister.
In the Commonwealth, the Queen's representative is the Governor-General.
In 2015 the Commonwealth Parliament abolished self-government on Norfolk Island and replaced its legislative assembly with a council.
Macquarie Island is administered by Tasmania, and Lord Howe Island is administered by New South Wales.
Jervis Bay Territory is a naval base and sea port for the national capital, on land that was formerly part of New South Wales.
Paterson's bush poem 'Waltzing Matilda' (1895) is regarded as Australia's unofficial national anthem.
Miles Franklin is the namesake of Australia's most prestigious literary prize, awarded annually to the best novel about Australian life.
Patrick White was the first recipient of the Miles Franklin prize and went on to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1973.
Australian winners of the Booker Prize include Peter Carey, Thomas Keneally and Richard Flanagan.
Many performing arts companies in Australia receive funding through the federal government's Australia Council.
Nellie Melba was one of the world's leading opera singers at the beginning of the 20th century.
Each state has a publicly funded theatre company, and there is a symphony orchestra in each state.
